title: Switch-like control of SREBP-2 transport triggered by small changes in ER cholesterol: a delicate balance
authors: Radhakrishnan A, Goldstein JL, McDonald JG, Brown MS
population: Chinese hamster ovary cell lines CHO-K1, CHO-7 and CHO-7 cells overexpressing human Insig-1
funder: Grants from the NIH (HL20948 and GM069338) and the Perot Family Foundation.
result: In purified ER membranes of CHO cells, resting ER cholesterol was about 7 mol% of ER lipids and whole-cell cholesterol about 35 mol% of cell lipids. SREBP-2 processing fell abruptly when ER cholesterol exceeded about 5 mol%; 50% inhibition occurred at 4.5 mol% (Hill coefficient 3.7) with cholesterol-cyclodextrin and at 5.7 mol% (Hill coefficient 3.5) with beta-VLDL in CHO-K1 cells, and at 5.5 mol% (Hill coefficient 5.1) in CHO-7 cells; the authors summarise the switch as 4.5-5.7 mol% with Hill coefficients of 3.5-5.1. About 6-fold overexpression of Insig-1 lowered the 50% inhibition point from 5.5 to 3.1 mol% and raised the Hill coefficient from 5.1 to 6.9.
